name: The Devolved
aliases: The ones that look like people
classification: Regressive Human Biological Derivative / Cognitive Reduction Experiment
origin_lab: Believed to originate from multiple labs independently, which makes them more disturbing than most single-origin specimens — the conditions that produce them are apparently reproducible. The most documented source is a developmental biology program operating under a legitimate academic grant studying 'cranial plasticity and cognitive threshold reduction in homo sapiens substrate,' which is a description that apparently cleared peer review. The program was investigating the theoretical lower bound of human cognitive function — how little brain could sustain a viable organism — with the long-term goal of producing low-maintenance biological labor. They found the floor. The floor walked out.
origin_method: Accelerated developmental regression via targeted suppression of frontal lobe growth factors combined with skeletal elongation therapy. The procedure was applied to embryonic or very early developmental substrate — the question of consent is therefore moot in a way that the researchers found convenient. The result is an organism that is human in origin, human in basic biology, and recognizably mammalian in body plan, but with a brain mass approximately 40% of typical human development, concentrated in the brainstem and limbic system, with the frontal cortex dramatically reduced. The skeletal structure develops abnormally under the elongation therapy: limbs are disproportionately long relative to the torso, with an arm-to-body ratio that reads as wrong before the observer can articulate why.
substrate: Human biological origin, developmental regression. Not posthuman in any augmented sense — pre-human in the specific sense of reduced cognitive architecture. They are warm-blooded, mammalian, require food and water and shelter, and breathe. They are also, by any clinical measure, not capable of the cognitive functions that distinguish adult human behavior. They operate on drives: hunger, shelter, temperature regulation, proximity to others of their kind.
physical_description:
At thirty meters in poor light, they look like a person who has been on the street for a long time. They are roughly human in height, upright, clothed in whatever has been accumulated, moving slowly in the hunched-shoulder gait of someone who has learned to occupy as little space as possible in a hostile environment. They are often in groups of two to four, which also reads as normal — small clusters of homeless individuals moving together for safety. Nothing about them at distance triggers alarm.

At ten meters, something is slightly wrong and the brain knows before the eyes can articulate it. The proportions are off. The arms hang too low. The neck is slightly too long, the head slightly too small for the body. The face is forward-pointing but the features are reduced — the brow is heavy, the eyes are set wider than normal, the jaw projects slightly. They do not make eye contact the way a person does.

At five meters, it is unambiguous. The arms reach the knee when relaxed at the side. The hands are large relative to the forearm. The skull is visibly reduced in the frontal regions, the forehead sloping back from the brow with no vertical height above it. The face does not produce the micro-expressions that human faces produce constantly in social interaction — the flickers of recognition, calculation, concern. It is a face that is doing something simpler than thinking.
behavioral_profile:
They eat. They sleep in clusters for warmth. They avoid loud noise and fast movement. They are not aggressive unless cornered, hungry, or — increasingly documented — defending something they have claimed, which might be a sleeping area, a food source, or another individual they have bonded with. In those circumstances they are capable of significant violence, not through planning or strategy but through the mammalian desperation of a large animal that sees no exit. Their strength is above average for their size — the elongated limb structure provides mechanical leverage that a standard human frame does not have.

The most unsettling behavioral characteristic, noted in every independent account from people who have had sustained contact with them, is that they watch. They do not stare in the fixed way of animals; they watch the way a person watches — tracking movement, noting behavior, orienting toward things that interest them. There is something in the limbic architecture that retained social attentiveness without retaining the cognitive equipment to do anything purposeful with the information. They notice things. They do not understand what they notice. They keep watching anyway.
threat_level: Low unless cornered or provoked. Moderate in groups, particularly if the group has bonded. Their size, strength, and the mechanical advantage of their limb proportions make a defensive encounter with three or more individuals genuinely dangerous. They are not tactical and they are not strategic. They are simply large warm animals that will fight if pushed far enough, and they do not read the social signals that tell a human observer how close to that threshold they are getting.
containment_status: Uncontained and extant in public. This is the definitional distinction between the Devolved and most other lab specimens — they are not in the dark. They are on the street. They move through the lower residential tiers and the approaches to the Undermarket and the margins of the Shelf district in clusters that are functionally invisible as long as they are at distance. The city's social infrastructure has accidentally provided them with cover: in a city where homelessness is extensive and visible, individuals and small groups who look like homeless people do not attract attention. The Devolved exploit this not through intent but through the accident of their appearance and behavior being a close-enough match to an existing ignored category.
known_locations: Lower residential tier approaches, specifically areas with transit flow and food service waste
The margins of the Shelf district, where residential and industrial zoning blur
Undermarket perimeter, particularly the loading corridor approaches
Several documented nesting sites in decommissioned utility structures adjacent to residential blocks
contamination_risk: No transmissible pathogen. The developmental regression process is not heritable in any documented case — the offspring of Devolved individuals, where this has been observable, develop normally, which produces its own set of tragic outcomes that are not well-documented because the cases tend not to surface through official channels. The risk is behavioral and social: they occupy space, they compete for resources, and their presence in a location causes escalating distress in human residents who begin to understand what they are looking at.
pacification_protocol: DPS Directive 4-B: Cognitive Regression Derivative. This directive has a classification flag that routes it to a secondary review channel before action is authorized, because the legal status of the Devolved — whether they qualify for protection as diminished-capacity humans or may be treated as hazardous fauna — has not been formally resolved. The flag was added after a DPS squad eliminated a group of nine in the lower tiers and a legal review determined that six of the nine had measurable residual human cognitive markers that might have cleared a threshold. Current status: observe and contain where possible, escalate to review before elimination, document all contact. In practice, the review process takes time that field teams do not have, and the documentation is often incomplete.
pitiable_qualities: They were people before the procedure. Not all of them — the embryonic-substrate cases never had cognitive development to lose — but a significant portion of the documented origin cases involved subjects who were adult or near-adult at the time of the experimental intervention, subjects who could be identified by family members if the records existed, which the labs ensured they do not. Somewhere in the behavioral residue of the Devolved, in the social attentiveness and the cluster-bonding and the watching, is the echo of what they were before someone decided their brain was more useful as a research variable than as a person. They are not suffering in any way they can articulate. They cannot articulate anything. But they watch the people moving around them with the persistent focused attention of something that remembers, at some unreachable depth, that this mattered.
story_hooks: A runner realizes the individual they have been passing every day at the transit corridor entrance — who they have been giving food to, who nods at them in what they have been interpreting as recognition — is not what they thought. The question of what to do with this realization has no clean answer.

A child in the lower residential block has been interacting with a group of Devolved in the utility corridor behind the building. The child does not find them frightening. The child has been feeding them for weeks. The parents have just found out.

A researcher has identified a Devolved individual who, based on bone structure, age, and a distinctive healed injury, matches the description of a missing person reported by a family six years ago. The family is looking for closure. The researcher is not sure closure is available in this form.
